target.title: RFC: add local adaptive-refresh replay tooling
target.body:
## Decision requested

Should CodexBar upstream own an offline CLI for comparing refresh policies against a caller-supplied JSONL trace?

`AdaptiveReplayCLI` is the only new product. Its supporting targets are package-internal. This PR does not make Adaptive the default or add a production signal. It remains an RFC because `VISION.md` requires owner sign-off for a new tool and its maintenance cost.

Refs #1739 and #1861.

## Scope after review

The first revision mixed offline analysis with runtime collection. That runtime scope is gone. This PR has no app recorder, trace writer, transcript scanning, provider calls, network path, or diagnostic storage lifecycle. It also removes the unrelated Keychain test change from the earlier branch.

The current three-way diff is 26 files and +3,036/-146. Tests account for 1,333 additions. The only production source change is a smaller `AdaptiveRefreshPolicy` adapter: +9/-44 in one file, with no scheduler, setting, provider, or policy-table change.

The JSONL parser also handles Swift CRLF graphemes with `Character.isNewline`. Strict and tolerant multi-record regressions cover the two Copilot findings.

## Shared policy architecture

The previous replay baseline copied the production policy table. This revision removes that second implementation.

Dependency direction:

- `CodexBar -> AdaptiveRefreshCore`
- `AdaptiveReplayCLI -> AdaptiveReplayKit -> AdaptiveRefreshCore`

`AdaptiveRefreshPolicyCore` is package-internal and Foundation-only. It is the only type that contains the adaptive thresholds, delays, precedence, and reason codes. The app adapter maps `ProcessInfo.ThermalState`; the replay adapter maps `ReplayThermalState` and converts the result for reporting.

`MirroredAdaptivePolicy` and its parity test are deleted. Coverage now follows ownership:

- core tests cover every table boundary, constrained-state precedence, future timestamps, the 2-30 minute bounds, and the five-minute heuristic interval;
- app adapter tests cover Darwin thermal-state normalization, timestamp forwarding, and nil history;
- replay adapter tests cover replay thermal-state normalization, output conversion, and interaction advances.

The scheduler integration, setting defaults, and provider behavior are unchanged.

## Data boundary

The CLI reads an explicit trace path and writes a report to stdout. Optional activity fields are input-only. No trace or fixture is committed. Runtime capture and its privacy/lifecycle contract remain out of scope.

## Author-run replay evidence

Exact head: `4709bec9ababdd2f605e1ec5330ee948bd166f49`

The local input has 1,780 records and SHA-256 `b1e4aa33180b7c177293eb9ed16b45e24e026d259600fba2b1b67b931b904f0b`. The raw trace remains local.

| Policy | Simulated refreshes | Per observed 24h | Simulated advances | Unconstrained active over 5m | Menu staleness p50 / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Current Adaptive | 694 | 143.47 | 53 | 4 / 145 | 142s / 1093s |
| Activity-cap candidate | 696 | 143.88 | 53 | 0 / 145 | 139s / 1093s |
| Fixed 5m | 1,383 | 285.90 | 0 | 0 / 99 | 150s / 281s |

The shared-core refactor produces the same replay result as the previous head. The run found 28 observed segments and excluded 26.10 hours with a five-minute legacy-gap heuristic. Activity fields were present for 462 of 733 decisions; 185 samples were inside the five-minute active window. The trace contains 46 recorded advances and zero timer-advance evaluations.

On this input, current Adaptive schedules 49.8% fewer simulated refreshes than fixed five minutes. The activity candidate adds two refreshes and removes four active-delay violations, but neither Adaptive variant improves p95 staleness. This does not support a default or production-policy change.

## Validation

For exact head `4709bec9`:

- 66 Adaptive replay/core tests passed across 8 suites.
- 4 macOS app-adapter tests passed.
- `swift build --product AdaptiveReplayCLI` passed.
- `swift run AdaptiveReplayCLI <hash-pinned-trace>` produced the table above.
- `make check` passed: SwiftFormat 0/1,375 and SwiftLint 0 violations in 1,374 files.
- `git diff --check` passed.

The previous head showed two red checks from one unrelated failure. The existing Kimi timing test measured 0.25113839 seconds against a strict `<0.250` assertion; the second red check was the aggregate gate reporting that shard failure. This PR does not change Kimi source or tests. The new head is running the CI matrix again.

## Limitations

- The replay evidence comes from one machine and the raw trace is not public.
- Gap segmentation is heuristic and cannot identify sleep, reboot, a long refresh, or an event-loop stall.
- The trace predates evaluation records, so accepted versus rejected live evaluations cannot be audited.
- The result does not measure battery use, elapsed user time, provider requests, or cost.
- Both Adaptive variants have worse p95 menu staleness than fixed five minutes on this trace.

The remaining decision is product ownership: should this repository maintain the offline CLI and its package-internal analysis targets?

target.title: fix(worker): count live reservations across months
target.body:
## Summary

- count live managed lease reservations in the active monthly budget window after UTC month rollover
- keep terminal prior-month reservations excluded from the current month
- cover fleet, owner, and organization caps at the month boundary
- document the enforcement semantics and credit the reporter

Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/1039

## Root cause

Cost-limit accounting filtered every reservation by its creation month. A lease still consuming provider capacity after rollover therefore stopped contributing to monthly reserved-USD caps until cleanup, permitting overlapping reservations above configured limits.

## Verification

- `npm test --prefix worker -- --run test/usage.test.ts`
- `npm run format:check --prefix worker`
- `npm run lint --prefix worker`
- `npm run check --prefix worker`
- autoreview: clean, patch correctness 0.97

target.title: [codex] Fix Claude auto fallback for MCP-only keychain
target.body:
## Summary

- Skip Claude OAuth during background `Auto` planning when cached Claude CLI credentials are expired and the live Claude Keychain contains MCP-only OAuth state.
- Fall through directly to the CLI/Web strategy instead of attempting an OAuth refresh that is known to fail.
- Preserve user-initiated refreshes, explicit OAuth mode, ordinary OAuth Keychain payloads, and disabled-Keychain behavior.
- Avoid the MCP-only Keychain probe when the Claude CLI fallback is unavailable.

## Verification

- [x] `swift test --filter ClaudeOAuthFetchStrategyAvailabilityTests` (17 tests)
- [x] `make check`
- [x] `make test` (605 selections, 51 groups)
- [x] Autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings

The test matrix uses no-prompt Keychain overrides and covers background Auto, user-initiated Auto, explicit OAuth, ordinary OAuth payloads, disabled Keychain access, unavailable CLI, and existing startup/prompt-policy paths.
